revenue: Total money a company brings in from selling its products or services before any costs are subtracted.
ebitda: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization — a rough measure of how much cash a business generates from operations.
gross margin: The percentage of revenue left after subtracting the direct cost of producing goods or services.
operating margin: The percentage of revenue left after paying all operating expenses, but before interest and taxes.
net margin: The percentage of revenue that remains as profit after all expenses, taxes, and interest have been paid.
roe: Return on equity — net profit expressed as a percentage of the shareholders' money invested in the company.
roa: Return on assets — net profit expressed as a percentage of total assets, showing how efficiently the company uses what it owns.
current ratio: Current assets divided by current liabilities — a measure of whether the company can pay its short-term debts.
quick ratio: Current assets minus inventory, divided by current liabilities — a stricter test of short-term financial health.
debt-to-equity: Total debt divided by shareholders' equity, showing how much the company relies on borrowing compared to owner funding.
p/e: Price-to-earnings ratio — the share price divided by earnings per share, indicating how much investors pay for each unit of profit.
p/b: Price-to-book ratio — the share price divided by book value per share, comparing market value to accounting value.
dividend yield: Annual dividend per share divided by share price, expressed as a percentage of what investors earn from dividends alone.
free cash flow: Operating cash flow minus capital expenditures — the cash left over after maintaining and expanding the business.
laba bersih: Net profit; the money remaining after every expense and tax has been subtracted from total revenue.
aset lancar: Current assets; resources the company expects to convert into cash within one year, such as cash, receivables, and inventory.
ekuitas: Equity; the portion of the company owned by shareholders, equal to total assets minus total liabilities.
laba ditahan: Retained earnings; accumulated profits that the company has kept rather than distributed as dividends.
pendapatan komprehensif lain: Other comprehensive income; gains and losses that affect equity but are not recorded in the main income statement.
catatan atas laporan keuangan: Notes to financial statements; detailed explanations and disclosures that accompany the main financial reports.
beban pokok penjualan: Cost of goods sold (COGS); the direct cost of producing the goods or services that were sold during the period.
arus kas dari aktivitas operasi: Operating cash flow; cash generated or used by the company's core business activities during the period.
working capital: Current assets minus current liabilities — the short-term funds available to run day-to-day operations.
accounts receivable: Money owed to the company by customers who bought goods or services on credit but have not yet paid.
accounts payable: Money the company owes to its suppliers for goods or services it has received but not yet paid for.
inventory turnover: How many times a company sells and replaces its inventory in a given period — higher is generally better.
asset turnover: Revenue divided by total assets, measuring how efficiently the company generates sales from its asset base.
interest coverage ratio: Operating profit divided by interest expense, showing how easily the company can pay interest on its debt.
debt service coverage: Net operating income divided by total debt service, measuring the company's ability to repay both principal and interest.
leverage ratio: A general measure of how much debt a company uses relative to its equity or assets.
book value: The net asset value of the company as recorded in its accounts — total assets minus total liabilities.
market cap: The total market value of all outstanding shares, calculated as share price multiplied by number of shares.
earnings per share: Net profit divided by the number of outstanding shares — the profit attributable to each single share.
price to sales: Share price divided by revenue per share, used to value companies that may not yet be profitable.
enterprise value: Market cap plus total debt minus cash — a measure of the company's total value including its debt obligations.
operating cash flow: Cash generated by the company's core business activities before accounting for financing or investing activities.
capex: Capital expenditure; money spent on buying or upgrading physical assets such as equipment, buildings, or technology.
depreciation: The gradual reduction in the book value of a tangible asset over its useful life, recorded as an expense.
amortization: The gradual write-down of intangible assets or loan costs over time, similar to depreciation but for non-physical assets.
goodwill: An intangible asset that arises when a company pays more than book value to acquire another company.
intangible assets: Non-physical assets with economic value, such as patents, trademarks, and brand recognition.
deferred tax: A tax liability or asset that arises when there is a timing difference between accounting profit and taxable profit.
minority interest: The portion of a subsidiary's equity not owned by the parent company, shown in consolidated financial statements.
retained earnings: Cumulative profits kept by the company over its history rather than paid out as dividends to shareholders.
shareholders equity: The total value belonging to shareholders, equal to total assets minus total liabilities.
treasury stock: Shares that the company has repurchased from shareholders and holds itself, reducing the number of outstanding shares.
gross profit: Revenue minus the cost of goods sold — the profit before operating expenses are deducted.
operating profit: Gross profit minus operating expenses such as salaries and rent — also known as EBIT.
net income: The final bottom-line profit after all revenues and expenses including taxes and interest have been accounted for.
comprehensive income: Net income plus other comprehensive income items such as foreign currency translation adjustments.
dividend payout ratio: The fraction of net income paid out as dividends to shareholders, expressed as a percentage.
payout ratio: Dividends per share divided by earnings per share, showing what share of profits is returned to investors.
sga: Selling, general and administrative expenses; overhead costs not directly tied to production, such as marketing and management salaries.
cost of revenue: The total direct cost incurred to deliver the products or services that generated the period's revenue.
gross profit margin: Gross profit divided by revenue, expressed as a percentage — measures production efficiency.
pendapatan: Revenue or income; the total amount earned by the company from its primary business activities during the period.
beban operasi: Operating expenses; costs incurred in running the business that are not directly tied to producing goods or services.
laba kotor: Gross profit; revenue minus the cost of goods sold, before deducting operating expenses.
laba operasi: Operating profit; gross profit minus operating expenses, also known as earnings before interest and taxes.
modal kerja: Working capital; the difference between current assets and current liabilities, used to fund day-to-day operations.
kewajiban lancar: Current liabilities; financial obligations the company must settle within one year.
kewajiban jangka panjang: Long-term liabilities; debt and other obligations due more than one year from the balance sheet date.
total aset: Total assets; the sum of everything the company owns — both current and non-current assets.
total liabilitas: Total liabilities; all financial obligations of the company, both short-term and long-term.
marjin laba kotor: Gross profit margin; gross profit expressed as a percentage of revenue, indicating production cost efficiency.
marjin operasi: Operating margin; operating profit expressed as a percentage of revenue, showing operational efficiency.
